title: Chicken Pox Vaccine
fit_question: Walk me through your resume. Why this firm?
prompt: A pharmaceutical company has completed phase two testing of a chicken-pox vaccine. Phase three would last two years, cost $300M, and has a 95% approval probability; production can begin immediately after approval. Should the company fund phase three?

clarifying_info.answer: One lifetime injection; US population 300M uniformly aged 0-75, with 4M entering and leaving annually; existing population can be vaccinated evenly over three years.
Per injection: $1.50 distribution, $2.50 production and $5 SG&A. The $300M phase-three cost includes all other setup and is expensed over testing.

interviewer_notes: Candidate-led, US-only. Key insight: after vaccinating the eligible existing population, volume falls to annual births. Show the two charts together but reveal willingness-to-pay only when pricing is requested.

suggested_framework.summary: Book framework covering market, economics and company fit.

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you decide whether to fund phase three?
stages.expected_answer: Size eligible existing and future patients, choose price from willingness to pay, calculate contribution and payback against $300M, probability-adjust if appropriate, and assess competitors and strategic fit.

stages.interviewer_asks: How many people are initially addressable?
stages.info_to_release: Population is 300M evenly distributed ages 0-75; vaccinate people with less than 50% infection probability. Exposure reaches 50% at age nine and 100% by 18.
stages.expected_answer: There are 4M people per age. Ages 0-18 total 72M; the under-nine half is 36M and considered not yet infected, so 36M are addressable.

stages.interviewer_asks: What price should the company charge?
stages.info_to_release: The willingness-to-pay curve remains high through $25 and is about 75% at $30 before dropping steeply.
stages.expected_answer: Charge $30: it is the inflection point, retains 75% adoption and gains $5 versus $25 before elasticity steepens.

stages.interviewer_asks: What are profit, recurring profit and breakeven?
stages.expected_answer: Eligible adopters are 36M×75%=27M, treated 9M/year for three years. Births add 4M×75%=3M/year, so the first three years after approval deliver 12M injections/year. Contribution is $30-$9=$21, or $252M/year and $756M over three years. Recurring profit after catch-up is 3M×$21=$63M/year. Simple payback of $300M at $252M/year is 1.19 years, not the book's approximate 1.25.

Yes. Price at $30, target ages 0-9, and fund phase three: post-approval contribution is $756M over three years, recurring profit $63M, and simple payback 1.19 years. Approval failure is 5%; protect rollout channels and monitor entry, although competitors face at least three years of earlier testing and miss the catch-up market.
good_answer_signals: Includes failure risk and competitor timing

exhibits.title: Cumulative Distribution of Chicken Pox Exposure
exhibits.description: Exposure rises from birth to 100% by age 18, crossing 50% near age nine.
exhibits.key_insight: Only the younger half of ages 0-18 is more likely uninfected than infected.

exhibits.title: Parents' Willingness to Pay
exhibits.description: Willingness to purchase by vaccine price, with about 75% at $30 and a sharp decline above it.

math.question: What is the addressable existing population?
What are profit and breakeven?
math.answer: $756M three-year profit, $63M recurring annual profit, 1.19-year payback
math.book_answer_if_different: The book reports approximately 1.25 years; its displayed $252M annual profit gives $300M/$252M=1.19 years.

synthesis: Fund phase three and price at $30. The catch-up market produces $756M contribution over three years, recurring births produce $63M annually, and simple payback is 1.19 years. Plan rollout and channels, account for 5% approval failure, and exploit the three-year testing lead before competitors can enter.

extraction.notes: Both candidate exhibits share page 90 and contain no answers. The printed 1.25-year payback is corrected to 1.19 years. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-09-30.
